Total bilirubin is 7 mg/dL with a direct (conjugated) fraction of 0.6 mg/dL (predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia). Onset after 24 hours of life, peak timing (~day 3–5) and modest bilirubin level are typical for physiologic neonatal jaundice. There is no evidence of hemolysis (Hgb 17.6 g/dL is normal for a newborn, reticulocyte count 0.3% is not elevated), and no clinical signs of significant anemia or hepatosplenomegaly. Although the mother is Rh-negative and the infant Rh-positive, there is no laboratory or clinical evidence of Rh hemolytic disease (which would present earlier, with higher bilirubin, anemia and elevated reticulocyte count). Feeding appears frequent, and there are no features of dehydration or altered stooling to suggest breastfeeding failure jaundice; breast milk jaundice typically appears later. Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and thyroid disease are not suggested by the data. Overall the timing, pattern, and labs are most consistent with physiologic neonatal (unconjugated) jaundice.

DIAGNOSIS: Physiologic neonatal jaundice (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia).
